title: Python basics: automation and AWS security utilities
objectives: Write a Python script that reads and parses a JSON API response.
Identify the security risk of hardcoding credentials in a script.

learningObjectives.statement: Write a Python script that reads and parses a JSON API response.
Identify the security risk of hardcoding credentials in a script.

body.value: Python is the primary scripting language for AWS security work. Boto3, the AWS SDK for Python, lets you query CloudTrail, inspect IAM policies, list S3 bucket permissions, and automate remediation — all from a script you can version-control and review.

Never hardcode AWS credentials in a script. Use IAM roles, environment variables loaded from Secrets Manager, or a credentials file with restricted permissions. A credential in source code is a credential that will eventually be exposed.

The same reasoning that applies to Linux file permissions applies to Python scripts: the script should request only the permissions it needs, read credentials from a controlled source, and leave no sensitive data in logs or temporary files.
